column2: You have set out to court [From.GetTitledFirstName], and one day, perhaps, to win [From.GetHerHis] hand. Among elves such things are not rushed: a courtship can last for years and is watched closely by every rival at court. How will you go on?
[From.GetFirstName] has married another. Any further courtship would have to be carried on in the shadows, and that is not what you set out to do.
You are married now. It would hardly be proper to go on courting [From.GetFirstName].
It was pleasant while it lasted.
Years wasted.
I will ask for [From.GetHerHis] hand.
I will ask for [From.GetHerHis] hand, in a matrilineal marriage.
A generous show of wealth will prove my devotion.
A show of my standing will prove my worth.
I shall court [From.GetHerHim] with poetry.
I shall court [From.GetHerHim] with the Winds of Magic.
I shall court [From.GetHerHim] with passion.
I shall hunt rare beasts for [From.GetHerHim].
I shall send [From.GetHerHim] the rarest blooms of my gardens.
I will show [From.GetHerHim] pleasures [From.GetSheHe] has never known.
I shall open my library to [From.GetHerHim].
I give up. [From.GetSheHeCap] is not worth it.

For months [From.GetTitledFirstName] has drowned you in gifts: gems from Caledor, silks from the harbours of Lothern, little caskets of gold that arrive with every ship. All of it in the hope of catching your eye.

For weeks [From.GetTitledFirstName] has made a show of [From.GetHerHis] influence. Acquaintances you barely know have come to speak of [From.GetHerHim] in glowing terms, and to tell you what a fine spouse [From.GetSheHe] would make.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has sent you another poem. You have lost count of how many delicate verses [From.GetSheHe] has written for you, each one more moving than the last.
Ribbons of light, flowers of frost that never melt, a songbird woven out of the Winds of Magic: [From.GetTitledFirstName] has given you quite a display of [From.GetHerHis] arts.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] corners you at every turn, whispering sweet words in your ear and drawing you into quiet alcoves. You have resisted [From.GetHerHis] advances so far, but is it really worth it?

Another rare pelt has arrived from [From.GetTitledFirstName], taken from [From.GetHerHis] latest kill. For weeks [From.GetSheHe] has filled your rooms with trophies of the hunt, every one of them taken in your honour, or so [From.GetSheHe] says.

Another bouquet has come from [From.GetTitledFirstName], so rare and lovely it might have been grown by Isha herself, with yet another invitation to walk in [From.GetHerHis] gardens. You wonder whether it would be proper to accept at last.

More than once in the past weeks [From.GetTitledFirstName] has dragged you into some wild revel that left you dizzy and aching by morning. At first it was unbearable, but you are starting to see how such things could become an acquired taste.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] is a meek suitor, if a suitor at all. All [From.GetSheHe] seems to want is to read with you and talk of the ancient sagas of your people, of Aenarion and Caledor and the Sundering.
I do like presents.
All of that is true.
That is sweet.
I am impressed.
Very well. Let us.
It is beautiful.
It does look enchanting.
Until tonight, then!
It is all so fascinating.
What a waste of money.
I am not interested.
How tedious.
Such reckless use of the Winds.
Perhaps another time.
So many wasted lives.
I have no time for such frivolities.
Enough of this.
What a bore.
You have spent a fortune on [From.GetFirstName], but [From.GetSheHe] plainly treasured many of your gifts. Showing that you can provide is the first stone in the foundation of any union.
Your attempt to impress [From.GetFirstName] worked perfectly. You had to call in many favours and have your friends slip into [From.GetHerHis] circle to sing your praises, but it was worth it.
You spent weeks writing verses for [From.GetFirstName], and at last [From.GetSheHe] has begun to warm to you. It was hard work, but you have caught [From.GetHerHis] attention.
[From.GetFirstName] was plainly enchanted by the spells you wove for [From.GetHerHim], one Wind after another, until [From.GetSheHe] could not look away.
[From.GetFirstName] could not have held out much longer. You used every art you have to charm [From.GetHerHim] these past weeks, and your efforts have finally borne fruit.
[From.GetFirstName] is taken with the trophies you sent [From.GetHerHim] from the wilds. You hear from more than one source that [From.GetSheHe] has been seen wearing your furs in public.
[From.GetFirstName] has finally come to walk your gardens. You lead [From.GetHerHim] through bower and glade and soon have [From.GetHerHim] enchanted by the wonders you have grown.
You have drawn [From.GetFirstName] into more than one wild revel these past weeks. At first [From.GetSheHe] kept to the edges, but now [From.GetSheHe] seems to enjoy celebrating excess at your side.
You have spent days with [From.GetFirstName], lost in old tomes and crumbling scrolls, studying the history of your people. You seem to have so much in common.
The courtship goes well.
For all your efforts and expense, [From.GetFirstName] has shown no interest at all in the gifts you have heaped upon [From.GetHerHis] house.
Your attempt to impress [From.GetFirstName] fell flat. For all the favours you called in, nobody could convince [From.GetHerHim] of your worth or your noble blood.
All the sleepless nights spent on verses for [From.GetFirstName] have come to nothing. [From.GetSheHeCap] remains cold to your poetry.
Not even the Winds of Magic can catch [From.GetFirstName]'s eye. Your many displays have left [From.GetHerHim] unmoved.
You tried every trick you know, but [From.GetFirstName] seems immune to your charms. Perhaps [From.GetSheHe] cares little for that side of a union.
[From.GetFirstName] did not even pretend to accept your last trophy. The pelt came back with a polite note asking you to stop. The hunt is plainly not to [From.GetHerHis] taste.
[From.GetFirstName] keeps ignoring your flowers and your invitations. [From.GetSheHeCap] says it is not a good time, but it may simply be that [From.GetSheHe] does not care for your gardens.
You tried to sway [From.GetFirstName] with wild feasts and heady wines, but [From.GetSheHe] has no taste for your kind of entertainment.
Your attempts to share the old scrolls with [From.GetFirstName] have failed. It seems [From.GetSheHe] has little interest in the ancient lore of the elves.
I must try something else.
You barely know each other, yet [From.GetTitledFirstName] has formally asked for your hand, in a matrilineal marriage.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has courted you for some time, so [From.GetHerHis] formal proposal of a matrilineal marriage comes as no great surprise.
You barely know each other, yet [From.GetTitledFirstName] has formally asked for your hand in marriage.
[From.GetTitledFirstName] has courted you for some time, so [From.GetHerHis] formal proposal of marriage comes as no great surprise.
I will take it to my liege.
No. I will not marry you.

[FromFrom.GetFirstName] has come to tell you that [From.GetTitledFirstName] has formally proposed a matrilineal marriage to [FromFrom.GetHerHim]. As [FromFrom.GetHerHis] liege, you must give or refuse your leave.
Your suitor, [From.GetTitledFirstName], has formally asked for your hand in a matrilineal marriage. The time has come to decide whether you will spend the rest of your long life together.
[FromFrom.GetFirstName] has come to tell you that [From.GetTitledFirstName] has formally proposed marriage to [FromFrom.GetHerHim]. As [FromFrom.GetHerHis] liege, you must give or refuse your leave.
Your suitor, [From.GetTitledFirstName], has formally asked for your hand in marriage. The time has come to decide whether you will spend the rest of your long life together.
I accept.
I cannot allow it.
Your proposal has been accepted! A great ceremony will soon bind you and [elfwed_beloved.GetFirstName] in marriage before the gods.
I am so happy!
[From.GetFirstName] has refused. All the years of courtship have come to nothing.
How could you?!

Elves from across the realm have come to your wedding. They congratulate you and your spouse, talk politics in the colonnades and listen to the music drifting through the air. The priests of many gods attend: Isha blesses the union with fertility, Lileath sends auguries of fortune, Asuryan counsels steady conduct, Vaul promises riches and Morai-Heg foretells long life. At each shrine you leave an offering and receive a blessing, and each binds you a little closer together.
And so we shall be.

The promise of life can only be bought with the certainty of death.\nTogether you and your spouse raise the still-beating heart of the sacrifice to the shrine of Khaine and let it burn under the gaze of the Lord of Murder, in the hope that it will slake his thirst and let your union bear fruit. Only a few chosen guests are invited, kept at a distance and watched by crossbowmen ready to loose at the first wrong move. When the first rite is over you leave the temple together, ready for a second, far more pleasurable one in honour of Atharti.
The gods are watching.

There is a season for everything. In the spring of this cycle you are joined with your spouse, but as every Asrai knows, this season too will pass, and one day you will be parted. Your union mirrors, in a small way, the sacred union of Isha and Kurnous, and like theirs your joy now will be balanced by sorrow to come. So the forest spirit reminds you as it gives its blessing and binds you together. Yet all cycles turn, and you will take what comes with a light heart and make the most of what you have.
We will.

[From.GetTitledFirstName] has decided to divorce you. One does not cast aside an Asur so lightly: as the wronged party, you may demand compensation in gold, or in land if [From.GetSheHe] has any to spare. Should [From.GetSheHe] refuse to pay, [From.GetHerHis] name will suffer for it.
I do not care. [From.GetSheHeCap] may go.
I demand gold for my trouble.
I demand land from [From.GetHerHis] demesne.
[From.GetFirstName] has let the divorce go through without asking for anything more than [From.GetHerHis] share of the costs.
It was good while it lasted.
[From.GetFirstName] is deeply wounded by the divorce. For [From.GetHerHis] cooperation, [From.GetSheHe] demands a heavy sum for [From.GetHerHis] broken heart and lost standing.
Very well.
I will not pay.
[From.GetFirstName] has given in to your demands. Once everything is signed and sealed, you are ready to say farewell to [From.GetHerHim] for good.
Good riddance.
[From.GetFirstName] has refused your demands.
Then go.
Then there will be no divorce!
[From.GetFirstName] took your refusal badly and has had the divorce struck down entirely. It seems you will be married a while longer after all.
Curses.
[From.GetFirstName] is deeply wounded by the divorce. For [From.GetHerHis] cooperation, [From.GetSheHe] demands part of your demesne as reparation for the damage done by your heartless soul.
As long as [From.GetSheHe] goes away.
I will do no such thing!
